label: paragraph_title
text: IF IT CAME.

label: text
text: Capt. Robert Dollar is somewhat of a national hero, not only on account of his organisation of a vast shipping concern with interests all over the world, but on account of the good work he has done in maintaining good relations between America and the nation's of the world, particularly China. It is interesting to recall that he was one of the first prominent American citizens to be approached regarding recognition of the Chinese Republic in

label: text
text: In the course of interviews within Mr. Yang Yao-sen and Mr. Tang Shao-yi at this time Captain Dollar warned them that the time was not ripe for inaugurating the new regime and that considerable difficulty would be experienced if the issue was forced before the people of China were educated up to a standard at which the working of a Republic would be possible.

label: text
text: Even more than his association with the Dollar shipping lines and the prominent part he was played in important world issues, Captain Dollar's genial and forceful personality is better known to the general public through the medium of the popular writer, Peter Kyne, who has made of him his hero, Cappy Ricks, figuring in a series of widely read stories dealing with life in the lumber fields.

label: text
text: Former Lumber Jack:

label: text
text:
It was as a number jack that Captain Robert Dollar first commenced his struggle in life and although his clever dealings since his rise to prosperity have stamped him as a man who was bound to rise very considerably from that estate it was a stroke of luck which first set "his foot on the ladder of success." As a skipper stranded without a cargo in the Philippines he risked taking a cargo of copra on his return to San Francisco—the first of its kind to be taken there. It caught on with the result that its export there has reached twenty million gold dollars a year.
Captain Dollar, although advanced in years, has preserved all those qualities of character and keen faculties which have enabled him to reach his present position. In appearance he is trim almost to elegance and it may be that in his very quietness and absence of bluster, the first thing which strikes one in conversation with him, lies the secret of getting through the work which "he recommends to the young man anxious to get on in the world." Work, hard work, and plenty of it is the only sure way to success is his advice.

LOCAL EXPERIENCE.

label: text
text: Since 1923, Hongkong has no. felt the full force of a typhoon. Then the wind velocity reached a record of 130 miles an hour. Some residents are anxious to know what conditions are like when in the thick of a cyclone.

label: text
text: Hitherto Mr. T. F., Olaxton, Director of the Royal Observatory, gave an idea of what would happen if a typhoon came to Hongkong.

label: paragraph_title
text: Central Calm Area.

label: text
text: The passage of the centre of a typhoon over two or more adjacent stations affords a means of determining the diameter of the calm area, which exists at the centre of a typhoon.

label: text
text: If for instance, at one station (A) the calm lasts for twenty minutes, while at another station (B) 2.4 miles to eastward the calm lasts 50 minutes and the typhoon is travelling north at the rate of 12 miles an hour, then the diameter of the calm area would be 12 miles.

label: text
text: At a third station (C) 9 miles to the east of (A) the calm would "would last 50 minutes also, but the wind would veer, whereas at A and B it would back, C being on the opposite side of the centre to A and B.

label: text
text: The centre calm, or eve of the storm as it is called, differs. in different typhoons. Its diameter varies from about 7 to 25 miles.

label: text
text: Sometimes an almost absolute calm occurs and sometimes light, variable winds are prevalent. Sometimes the skies clear completely sometimes partially and sometimes the heavy nimbus merely gives way to a veil of thinner cloud.

label: text
text: The barometric minimum (which varies from 27 inches to 29 inches) is said to occur sometimes at the beginning of the calm, sometimes shortly before, and sometimes shortly after; but as the time-scale of the ordinary barograph is usually very contracted and the driving clock an imperfect timekeeper, it is frequently impossible to say within 5, 10, or even 15 minutes, when the minimum pressure occurs. Probably it is within a few minutes of the calm. When the diameter of the calm area is large, and the sky clears, the temperature rises as the centre passes, otherwise there is no perceptible change.

label: text
text:
Typhoons vary considerably in strength. In some the violence of the winds even 100 miles from the centre beggars description while in others a vessel may pass actually through the centre without sustaining serious damage.
On June 2, 1916, the Observatory in Kowloon was on the edge of the calm centre of a small typhoon, moving north-east and evidently filling up. The wind, which had been strong to fresh, died away completely between 1 p.m. and 2 p.m. increasing again with fresh squalls from northward by 4 p.m. No damage was done. In contrast to this may be mentioned the Mauritius typhoon of April 29, 1892, in which 10,000

label: text
text: people were killed.

label: text
text: In those days little was known by the public about typhoons, and the central calm was mistaken for the end of the storm. People therefore opened hurricanes shutters, and left their houses, some never to return and others to find them in ruins, or blown to another street by the terrific hurricane which followed the central calm.

label: text
text:
Even if fully prepared Hongkong would suffer considerably, should the centre of a severe typhoon pass over the Island.
Ancient (and some modern) houses would collapse and probably a certain portion of the ships in shelter would be blown ashore and their decks swept clean. Many trees would be blown down. The greatest danger to pedestrians would be from tiles and corrugated iron hurtling through the air.

label: paragraph_title
text: PERJURY.

label: paragraph_title
text: DRAFT OF NEW BILL.

label: text
text: A Bill to amend the Perjury Ordinance it is proposed to introduce into the Legislative Council shortly.

label: text
text: This Bill proposes to effect a minor amendment in the Perjury Ordinance, 1922. Section 10 of that Ordinance makes it possible, when a witness has made two contradictory statements, to charge him with having made the contradictory statements and to obtain a conviction on proof of this contradiction without the necessity of proving the truth or falsehood of either statement. This section originally appeared as a section 6 of Ordinance No. 7 of 1857. Section 12 of the Perjury Ordinance gives a Judge or Magistrate power to direct a prosecution for perjury and to commit the accused for trial or to admit to bail. There is no similar power to order a prosecution for an offence against section 10. Clause 2 of the Bill proposes to give this power.

London! July 30.
The National Miners' Delegate Conference in London considered the reports from districts, particularly the Midlands, where, it was declared, the drift-buck to work has now practically stopped, and they also discussed the memorandum of the proposals of the Bishops and Free Church leaders, providing an immediate resumption on pre-stifle conditions, and a negotiation of a national settlement within four months, the disagreements existing thereafter to be referred to an arbitrator.

label: text
text: Mr. Cook and other leaders, however, advised the delegates that the Federation did not agree with the question of house being referred to an arbitrator---Reuter.

label: text

label: text

label: text

label: text

label: paragraph_title
text: COMING VOTE.

label: paragraph_title
text: What it Means to Both Sides.

label: text
text: At the conference of miners' delegates which was held to-day Mr. Herbert Smith, President of the Miners' Federation, called upon the delegates to give reports on the position in their districts and the numbers of men who had returned to work. It is stated that it was found that in the aggregate 6,100 men had resumed work in all the coal fields, excluding safety men. The men who had returned were not necessarily coal, getters, but generally embraced every class of mine workers.

label: text
text:
There was afteryard a discussion on the general position and on the recommendation of the Executive that the peace proposals framed in conjunction with the Bishops and the Free Church leaders should be accepted.
It is understood that the discussion was at times very animated. The Executive had ruled out of the proposals any arbitration on the question of hours, but delegates from some of the larger districts are stated to have objected also to arbitration on wage reductions.
At the close of the conference, however, it was officially stated that it had been decided by a very large majority to send the proposals to the districts to be voted upon, with a recommendation that they be accepted.

label: text
text: Whatever may be the result of the district vote, there will remain the fact that the primary proposal is that work shall be resumed for a period of four months at the old rate of wages whilst negotiations are proceeding, and that financial assistance shall be given by Government for this purpose. The Government has definitely stated that no such further subsidy or loan is possible. If the vote is favourable, however, it will at least mean that positive proposals have been substituted for the negative declarations of the miners' lenders, which have hitherto stood in the way of negotiations.—British Wireless Service.
